This build contains many differences, cut content, as well as **debug symbols!** It was built around 5 months before the game went gold and around 45 days after the first trailer, so it is _quite_ unstable and requires **a lot** of patches. ## Contents - [1Notes](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Notes) - [2Cuts](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Cuts) - [3Differences](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Differences) - [4Soundtrack](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Soundtrack) - [5Known issues](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Known_issues) - [6Screenshots](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Screenshots) - [7Origin](https://hiddenpalace.org/Midnight_Club_3:_DUB_Edition_(Oct_24,_2004_Prototype)#Origin) ## Notes - This build has a **dongle requirement**, a **memory leak**, and a few other issues. PNACH files to get around these issues have been uploaded as well as a cheat to unlock all cars. Thanks to **Devildwarf** and **Ghostie** for providing these. - Found by [u/MommysSalami near San Diego](https://archive.ph/R1ZCA) - The build was made by a QA employee that wanted to keep a version containing his favorite bug (allowing one to **slingshot** their car across the map while **drifting a certain way**) before it got patched. - This could be referring to **fishtailing**, a well-known exploit enabling players to accumulate extreme speed during drifts in Midnight Club II. This exploit was noticeably nerfed in the retail build but is far more powerful in this build. - They also mentioned that **more than one** build has been made by that QA employee. - Executable is named **SLUS\_123.45**, save says it's **SLUS\_202.10**, which is just the next serial code after Midnight Club II's **SLUS\_202.09** - All videos are placeholders - Intro movies are actually from Midnight Club II - Tutorial movies are videos of Rockstar logos rotating to the sound of a vehicle starting up with radio playing Limp Bizkit's _[Rollin' (Urban Assault Vehicle)](https://youtu.be/ADSTD-MprPs?si=nn_8_8Ej0o3Ek6Re&t=25)_, meanwhile police sirens and barking dogs can be heard in the distance. - An example of such a tutorial video can be seen [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HQL4iNclSfQ) - Use quickbms and Dave.bms script to extract DAT archive files - see [here](https://zenhax.com/viewtopic.php@t=17531.html). Alternatively you can use DAVE.py (requires [python](https://www.python.org/)) \- see [here](https://ednessp.github.io/tools#Midnight_Club) - Cheat codes in this version: - normal - Says "!!CC\_DEFAULTABILITIES!!", seems to revert the cheats below(?) - roar - Says "!!CC\_ALLROAR!!", enables roar for all cars - agro - Says "!!CC\_ALLAGRO!!", enables agro for all cars - zone - Says "!!CC\_ALLZONE!!", enables zone for all cars - allcash - Says "!!CC\_ALLCASH!!", sets your money to 4,200,000 - cars - Says "!!CC\_VECHICLES!!", unlocks all cars - parts - Says "!!CC\_PARTS!!", unlocks all cars parts - cities - Says "!!CC\_CITIES!!", unlocks all cities - cash - Says "JACKPOT", sets your money to 4,200,000 - all - Says "UNLOCKALL", does what it says - trythisathome - Says "!!CC\_OK!!, seems to do the same as the final version (bikers has flames on head) - Relevant memory addresses: - Debug info can be enabled by setting **00690EAC** to 1 or 2 or **00690EB0** to 1. - Address for editing money is **2BFEE44D3CC** ## Cuts - A **cut song** was found in this build's [string table](https://hiddenpalace.org/File:MC3Oct2004StringTable.zip) \- Yung Wun's _[Tear It Up](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mK9tujntNj0)_ - Limp Bizkit's _Rollin' (Urban Assault Vehicle)_ can also be a cut song since it's used in all placeholder videos. - A **cut vehicle** is in this build - a 2004 _Maybach 57_. - It was already known by the community to be cut and [even discussed by Kris Roberts 4 months before this build was released](https://youtu.be/sXZsg9xY9_Y?si=PSMusd7UnDLRizbi&t=831). - It can be driven and is listed in the garage, however going into body parts customization crashes the game and its UV texture across the hood, sunroof and trunk is broken, causing vinyls and damage to display incorrectly. - A **cut character** named **Dante** driving a _Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR_ in each city. - Internally referred to as the World Champ. - In the retail build, Lamont drives a _Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR_ in Atlanta. - Cars also don't make any sounds when hitting other vehicles or walls. - Almost no voice acting in this build - only pedestrians have lines. - Some songs are uncensored (e.g. Trick Daddy's _Let's Go,_ Hundred Reasons's _Stories With Unhappy Endings_ and Peaches's _Kick It_), some have different mixes (Trick Daddy's _Jump On It_ has a slightly different chorus) and some are full versions of the songs (e.g. Dark Energy's _Nitestrike_ and Galaxy 2 Galaxy's _Hi-Tech Jazz_) instead of shortened ones like in the retail build. - No genre selection in the audio options. - Gameplay: - Explosions' slow-mo takes far longer to end. - Car physics are different - they roll more often, feel less weighty and are less "glued" to the road. - Hitting opponents with a car while looking for a race doesn't activate them. - Phil is called C.J. in this version. - Hookmen during a race are unmarked - You have to press the button for changing camera POV to skip a race intro. - Hidden Rockstar logos don't disappear when hit in Atlanta or Detroit. They behave like any other physics object. - Some races that have cop chases in the retail build don't have them in this build - Racers have a dialogue for when you arrive at a race start - If you arrive first, they will say "Not bad! Lets race!" - If they arrive first, they will say "Better drive faster in the race" - There are no cutscenes with a countdown girl/guy. - Autocross races are different: - You can use nitro. - No target time shown during the race. - They are easily won as the finish time of other opponents is around 15 minutes, while you can easily finish the lap in 1-2 minutes. - Cop vehicles can be used in Career mode - Cars: - Some cars' manufacturer vinyls have different designs. - Many price differences, e.g. SLR Vision costs $1,600,000 instead of $452,750 - Tuners' trim colors can be changed. - Headlights don't show on the ground. - Also, their lens flare is different -- far more sharp. - If headlight meshes from this build are added to the retail build, they appear quite distinct from the final ones, notably having a separation between the lights. See [here.](https://hiddenpalace.org/File:MC3Oct2004Headlights.png) - Manual transmission can't be used without patches. - Cities: - All billboards are stand-ins (with custom artwork by Rockstar) that were replaced with commercials for e.g. album releases, products like Pepsi or TV channels. - Train model in San Diego is different - doesn't have transparent windows. - Train model in Detroit is different - has transparent windows, but no passengers inside. - Lighting on maps is more pronounced. A lot more lightmaps and contrast overall. - Culling is very buggy and some parts of the map can't be seen despite nothing blocking the view. - Pedestrians can jog and walk through crossings - Pedestrian density is also far higher compared to the retail build and also can be modified in arcade mode, setting to none will still enable em. - Some places in-game were renamed, possibly to minimize association with real-life businesses, e.g. [SeaLand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SeaWorld_San_Diego "wikipedia:SeaWorld San Diego") into Water Park or [Omni Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omni_San_Diego_Hotel "wikipedia:Omni San Diego Hotel") into just Hotel. - Many wooden posts have powerlines that connect to other wooden posts. - Some hidden Rockstar logos are missing. ## Soundtrack - All music playlists are the same in every city - in the frontend, in the garage, during a race or while cruising, except after a race ends. Their content is as follows: - The Martian - Lost Transmission From Earth - Suburban Knight - Nightstrike - The Martian - Star Dancer - Underground Resistance - I'm In - Underground Resistance - Amazon - The Aztec Mystic - Jaguar - Underground Resistance - Jupiter Jazz - Suburban Knight - Nocturbulous - The Martian - Sex In Zero Gravity - The Aztec Mystic - Aguila - Suburban Knight - The Warning - The Martian - Search Your Feelings - Underground Resistance - Hi-Tech Jazz - Underground Resistance - Return of the Dragons - Orlando Voorn - Bite Before You Bark - Fix - Flash - The Tek Brothers - Denang - B. Calloway - Direct Maniac - Underground Resistance - Windchime - Apathy - Drive It Like I Stole It - Fix - Flash (yes, it repeats for some reason and has two separate files) - Grim Northerns - Urban Pressure - Hundred Reasons - Stories With Unhappy Endings - Peaches feat. Iggy Pop - Kick It - Trick Daddy feat. Khia & Tampa Tony - Jump On It - Trick Daddy feat. Twista & Lil Jon - Let's Go - Music playlists that play when you finish a race are different though, but are the same whether you win or lose. Their content is as follows: - Funeral for a Friend - Escape Artists Never Die - Fat Joe feat. M.O.P. & Petey Pablo - Fight Club - Trick Daddy feat. Birdman - Gangsta - Nappy Roots - Hustla - Trick Daddy feat. Lil Jon & Twista - Let's Go - Jazze Pha - Materialistic - Fat Joe - My Lifestyle - Fat Joe feat. Remy Ma - Opposites Attract - Damageplan - Pride - Authority Zero - Revolution - Damageplan - Save Me - Twista feat. R. Kelly - So Sexy ## Known issues Some of these issues are fixed or mitigated by patches linked at the top of this page. Please do not run this build without patches or without reading this list first. - Runs terribly on PCSX2's hardware rendering with default settings - either play on software rendering, downgrade PCSX2 to v2.2.0 or disable depth conversion, partial source invalidation and enable "estimate texture region" in manual hardware renderer fixes. An early prototype of Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition for the PlayStation 2.
This build contains many differences, cut content, as well as debug symbols! 
It was built around 5 months before the game went gold and around 45 days after the first trailer, so it is quite unstable and requires a lot of patches...
